idiom_name: Exposed DSL select/where over JDBC (or JPA Criteria on the JVM)
implementation_notes: Kotlin/JVM takes the query object from the persistence library: Exposed's DSL composes typed statements over Table objects (Users.selectAll().where { Users.status eq "active" }) and the returned Query accepts andWhere/orderBy/orWhere for optional filters, while the JPA Criteria API is available unchanged because Kotlin compiles to bytecode. What replaces the classic structure is a library DSL plus Kotlin lambdas and extension functions; a hand-built query abstraction stays justified only when it must stay independent of the ORM, at the price of giving up schema typing.
pitfalls: An Exposed Query is bound to the transaction that built it: composing in one transaction and executing in another targets the wrong connection.
JPA string attributes (root.get<String>("age")) lose compile-time safety in Kotlin too - prefer the generated metamodel or a typed DSL.
Lazy JPA entities copied into data classes are the usual source of N+1; plan fetch joins when a query result feeds a DTO.
